name: Production Payment Orchestrator
tagline: Operate a payment switch through changing production incidents.
narrative:
You own the policy for a national payment switch. The stream contains retail transfers, refunds, payroll, business payments, merchant settlements, and cross-border traffic.

Providers have different capabilities and can fail, recover, slow down, or run out of capacity. Failed payments may be retried, but retries consume time and can push urgent work past its deadline. Submit runs the same policy against protected scenarios that deliberately change the visible assumptions.
objective: Balance throughput, cost, reliability, deadlines, retries, compatibility, congestion, and customer impact across the visible and hidden runs.
learningObjective: Design a production-grade policy for delayed feedback, changing capacity, mixed traffic, and conflicting service goals.
intelligenceExplanation:
The engine exposes the current payment, retry history, deadline, and provider facts. Your route starts asynchronous processing; later observations show the capacity consumed by earlier choices.

Hidden scenarios change provider identity, traffic mix, health schedules, prices, deadlines, and value restrictions. A policy that memorises one visible route will not generalise.
hint: Build the policy in layers: eligibility, deadline safety, retry diversity, urgency, then cost and load optimisation. Give the final fallback a deliberate meaning.
hints: Never route without canRoute. Use transaction-type and value facts indirectly through canRoute rather than duplicating provider contracts.
Use lastProvider and retryCount to prevent repeated failure on one rail; use deadlineRemaining to decide whether holding or another attempt is still defensible.
A robust policy reserves reliable low-latency capacity for urgent/high-impact traffic and spreads flexible traffic across healthy eligible providers before congestion cascades.
brief: Build one general policy for high-volume traffic, failures, retries, and deadlines.
context: Each decision changes future capacity while providers process payments in parallel and new events arrive.

steps.label: Encode eligibility, compatibility, amount, capacity, and deadline invariants
Treat retail, refund, payroll, business, settlement, international, high-value, and urgent traffic intentionally
Use live congestion, health, latency, and retry history instead of static provider preference
Pass the ten-case adversarial submission suite

objectives.label: Keep visible timeouts at or below 5
Keep visible priority failures at or below 2
Keep overload rejections at or below 3
Keep the visible penalty score below 300

rubric: Outage, recovery, congestion, and retry resilience: 25%

goals.description: Protect customer outcomes while sustaining national-switch throughput.

states.description: Continuously observe and control the payment switch.

functions.description: Attempt the current payment through Provider A.
Attempt the current payment through Provider B.
Attempt the current payment through Provider C.
Wait one tick while the production environment continues evolving.
Permanently decline the current payment when no safe service path remains.
